parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes traveller-facing exposure at entry, in facilities, and in custody. Parent screening can refuse cases or find fraud for sex-document discrepancies, and reports describe passport confiscation; the division mandates birth-sex facility use, shelter exclusion and prison placement, with a criminal drag/impersonation ban and no working facility remedy. National custody practices and immigration detention are documented as abusive. Some protections exist (national hate-crime coverage, court challenges, X passports valid until expiry), but they do not reach the division's facility and custody rules. The result is High Risk, short of the imprisonment-likely anchor but materially worse than denial-of-entry-only cases.

entry_documents.exposure: Parent screening may refuse cases with document or record discrepancy and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility for suspected sex misrepresentation; X markers no longer issued; reports of confiscated passports and stranded travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; policy is in litigation; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Passport/presentation mismatch can lead to secondary screening, refusal, or fraud finding; division document closure compounds mismatch.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men; corrections bureau conversion practices; division prisons place by birth sex and bar inmate care.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; no division custody remedy documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest or immigration hold flows into birth-sex custody with documented harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Parent bars gender-congruent federal single-sex facilities; division requires birth-sex facilities and bars trans women from shelters.
federal_state_facilities.protection: None documented operating for trans visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State and federal facility rules reinforce exclusion; no working remedy.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for minors and inmates, with regret suits and provider penalties; parent hostile to minors' care and trans health funding.
care_services.protection: Adult routine care not shown barred; court injunctions block some national measures.
care_services.interaction: Minor traveller or emergency/custody care encounters restrictions; adult care uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; division criminalises drag/impersonation where a child could see; indecent-exposure definition exists but enforcement unsourced.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute; some court blocks.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing raises official suspicion; division performance law can criminalise public gender expression.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division bans care for under-18, requires school outing, restricts sport by birth sex, allows regret suits; parent executive order threatens teachers over social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Some national orders enjoined; no division protection documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling minor with trans presentation faces facility rules and care denial; guardian exposure via assistance penalties.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division lacks gender-identity hate-crime coverage; gay/trans panic defence available; reports of police indifference and anti-LGBTQ assaults/discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; prosecutor opinion allows gender enhancement.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Outing can leave victim with weak local recourse; national statute partial.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: 2026 facility/shelter and prison provisions' enforcement or challenge status unsourced; licence-marker suit outcome unknown; drag-ban separate suit pending.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National courts have enjoined some parent orders; legal aid tracks passport rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertain enforcement means exposure persists but exact visitor experience varies.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A involves invasive administrative review and denial of entry, with no imprisonment. This dossier is lower: it adds universal birth-sex facility exclusion, shelter exclusion, birth-sex custody placement and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, though it lacks the anchor's explicit no-detention guarantee.

0.25-A centres coercive detention and extortion over document mismatch. This dossier has less documented street-level extortion but more state-imposed facility and custody exposure, including a criminal drag ban and prison placement by birth sex.

0.55-B has a functioning protection that eventually clears the traveller, with only administrative uncertainty. Here no working division remedy offsets facility and custody rules, so it sits materially below.

0.15-A posits imprisonment highly likely and possible execution for identity misrepresentation. This dossier lacks execution and routine imprisonment for trans identity, so it is well above that extreme, but entry fraud and custody harm keep it in High Risk.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is not a single national rule but an interaction: a trans visitor's document mismatch can trigger parent secondary screening or a fraud finding; once in the division, birth-sex facility and shelter rules create universal exclusion, and any custody moves into birth-sex prison placement with documented national abusive practices. National hate-crime coverage and court injunctions are real but partial; they do not repair division facility or custody rules. Violence data are too thin and undercount-dependent to carry weight, but panic defence and police indifference reduce recourse. Overall High Risk.
